neighbours.label: the fused sentence-end-plus-newline token '.\n' closing a factual line in prose
fire:
The museum opened in 1931 after a long public campaign.
Its first director was a retired sea captain.

The plant flowers only once every few years.
The blooms last about a week.

Your pharmacist can answer questions about side effects.
Keep this leaflet for later.

The train line was extended to the airport in 2004.
Ridership doubled within a year.

Our dog refuses to walk in the rain.
He waits by the door until it stops.

The plane was retired from service in 1991.
It now stands outside the visitor center.

The committee approved the budget on Tuesday.
Work on the new library will begin in spring.

The castle was rebuilt twice in the fifteenth century.
Only the north tower survives today.
quiet: The museum opened in 1931 after a long public campaign, and its first director was a retired sea captain.
The plant flowers only once every few years, and the blooms last about a week.
Your pharmacist can answer questions about side effects, so keep this leaflet for later.
The train line was extended to the airport in 2004, and ridership doubled within a year.
Our dog refuses to walk in the rain and waits by the door until it stops.
The plane was retired from service in 1991 and now stands outside the visitor center.
The committee approved the budget on Tuesday, so work on the new library will begin in spring.
The castle was rebuilt twice in the fifteenth century, but only the north tower survives today.
